declarations.en: For an arbitrary number field F and y ∈ F, normalize a finite-place absolute value by |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At infinite places use real absolute values and complex moduli with weights mw = 1 and 2. Set log⁺ t = max(0,log t), using the total real logarithm with log 0 = 0. Let hfin,F(y) be the sum of log⁺|y|v over ALL finite places of F, hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). The sums define relative logarithmic heights, without division by [F:Q]; the corresponding absolute logarithmic height is hrel,F(y)/[F:Q]. Define hinf,F(y) = Σw mw log⁺|y|w.

declarations.en: Let λ be an element of the fixed algebraic closure Q̄ of Q with λ ≠ 0,1, let x denote this point, and let Fλ = Q(λ) be the full simple subfield of Q̄ generated by λ. All occurrences of λ inside height and place expressions mean the canonical generator in Fλ. Put dλ = [Fλ:Q] = degree of the minimal polynomial of λ. At a finite place v corresponding to a nonzero prime ideal 𝔭 of the ring of integers of Fλ, use |y|v = N(𝔭)^(−ord𝔭(y)) for y ≠ 0 and |0|v = 0. At an infinite place w use the usual real absolute value or complex modulus with multiplicity mw = 1 or 2, respectively. Write log⁺ t = max(0, log t), with the total real logarithm log 0 = 0. Define hfin,F(y) = Σ over ALL finite places v of F of log⁺|y|v, hinf,F(y) = Σ over infinite places w of F of mw log⁺|y|w, and hrel,F(y) = hinf,F(y) + hfin,F(y). These are relative heights, with no division by [F:Q]. The absolute logarithmic point height is hcan(x) = hrel,Fλ(λ)/dλ. Set Jλ = 256(λ²−λ+1)³/[λ²(λ−1)²] and a(x) = hfin,Fλ(Jλ)/dλ. In particular, a(x) uses Fλ, which need not be Q(Jλ). All logarithms are natural. A bounded-set datum K consists of a finite set V of rational prime numbers with 2 ∈ V and a real number c, with no separate axiom c ≥ 0. A point belongs to K precisely when |log|λ|v| ≤ c and |log|λ−1|v| ≤ c for every finite place v of Fλ whose residue characteristic belongs to V, and the same two bounds hold for EVERY infinite place of Fλ. Finite places with residue characteristic outside V are not constrained by membership in K; they are still included in every finite-height sum.
